Hi James / team,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clarity on your ramp profile across Q3–Q4. Attached is the clean Master Services Agreement and the prepay schedule we discussed (3-year, annual prepay with ramped capacity and a 20% term discount baked into year 1 pricing). Key points: 

- Prepay structure: Year 1 upfront (committed tokens) + optional annual true-up each renewal.
- Early termination: Standard clause allows return of unearned prepay on a pro rata basis; we included a typical 90-day notice requirement.
- Co-terming: We can co-term smaller subsidiaries to the parent contract on Year 2 with a small administrative fee.

I've attached the Redwood_SA_20270409.pdf and a simple amortization spreadsheet. Can you review the SA and the prepay numbers and send any redlines by early next week? If procurement wants an escrow mechanism for unused funds, we can discuss options — we usually see either (a) refund schedule, (b) escrow with release milestones, or (c) amortization with no escrow if there are strong forecasting commitments.

Next step: If procurement and finance are aligned, I'll route to our legal ops for a short co-term amendment and DocuSign.

Best,

Rachel — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed with procurement and finance. A few redlines and asks attached (ACME_Redlines_20270409.docx). High level: 

1) Early termination/refund: We cannot accept full pro rata returns for prepay without an escrow or locked schedule; our procurement needs a staged refund tied to usage milestones (e.g., 25% after 6 months, 50% after 12 months, remainder on pro rata amortization).
2) Escrow: They want an escrow for amounts above $250k in Year 1, with release to Redwood on a quarterly basis as services are consumed or milestones met.
3) Co-terming: Request to co-term three subsidiaries in Year 2 with consolidated reporting and a single payment. Prefer no administrative fee, but open to a nominal fee.
4) Renewal credits: If we extend early, they want renewal credits applied to remaining prepay value.

Can your legal/finance confirm escrow logistics (custodian options, fees) and a conservative refund waterfall? Procurement also called out revenue recognition — they prefer an amortization schedule that lines up with our FY.

James

Rachel — thanks for flagging. Quick thoughts: 

- Escrow: We can offer an escrow for amounts >$250k, but recommend using a neutral custodian with quarterly releases tied to reported consumption. Redwood should retain right to audit consumption logs (token-level) before release. Custodian candidates: PrimeTrust, BitGo (for cash equivalents), or a bank escrow. Ops will need a fee schedule (typically 0.2–0.5% p.a.).

- Refund waterfall: Counter-proposal: 40% refundable in Year 1 (subject to 90-day notice), 30% refundable in Year 2, remainder amortized monthly thereafter. For early termination due to Redwood breach, full pro rata refund applies. This caps exposure while giving Acme protection.

- Co-terming: Acceptable if subsidiaries sign guarantees and provide consolidated PO; we should preserve Redwood's right to chase payment at the parent level. No admin fee, but require a one-time amendment to add entities and align billing.

I'll draft clause language for legal to insert into the SA. Karthik — can you weigh in on the guarantee wording? Kimberly — please confirm revenue recognition and whether amortization monthly aligns with our ASC guidance and how refunds impact deferred revenue.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME redlines — escrow + staged refund asks

Following up on Vanessa's note with finance perspective: 

- Amortization: Monthly amortization across the contract term works fine for revenue recognition. If we hold an escrow, Redwood must treat escrowed cash as restricted until release; we can only recognize revenue on amounts out of escrow once released or upon verified consumption.

- Refund cap: The proposed 40/30/30 split is acceptable operationally; recommend we add a clawback provision if usage materially deviates (>30% lower than forecast for two consecutive quarters).

- Accounting ops: If Acme requests co-terming and consolidated payment, we need a signed parent guarantee and a consolidated billing addendum for our records (keeps audit trail clean).

I'll attach a sample amortization table and a suggested escrow fee band for inclusion.

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance (Revenue)

James — appreciate the detailed feedback and redlines. We've reviewed internally and propose the following counter to your procurement asks: 

1) Escrow: We agree to an escrow for Year 1 amounts >$250k with quarterly releases tied to verified consumption. Redwood requests audit rights over consumption logs prior to each release. Suggested escrow custodian candidates are listed; we can include a 0.35% p.a. fee to the deal as a pass-through.

2) Refund waterfall (counter): 40% refundable in Year 1 (90-day notice), 30% refundable in Year 2, remainder amortized monthly. For termination due to material Redwood breach, we will make refunds pro rata without cap. We will include a 30% deviation clawback if actual consumption is >30% below your forecast for two consecutive quarters.

3) Co-terming: We can co-term the three subsidiaries in Year 2 with no admin fee provided the parent signs a guarantee and a consolidated PO is submitted at amendment. We'll prepare a short amendment template for signature.

4) Renewal credits: If Acme opts into an early renewal, any unused prepay remaining will be applied as a credit toward the renewal at the contracted unit price.

If you can confirm acceptance of these points, I will circulate a redline to the SA and the amendment for co-terming and route for DocuSign. Proposed timeline: counter and DocuSign by EOD Thursday to hit your procurement window.

Thanks, and happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
